title: I get AI to review my videos
hook: I'm using AI to look at my competitors
summary: How to use AI to review your own videos (and learn from the creators you admire)
body: How to use AI to review your own videos (and learn from the creators you admire)
I was watching way more of other people's content than I was making my own. So I turned that into a system:

1. Give AI the creators you respect and ask what makes their videos work
2. Turn that into a checklist of hooks, pacing and style
3. Have AI review MY videos against it: "do this, stop doing that"
Comment REVIEW and I'll send you the prompt.
guide: Use AI to study creators you admire, turn what you learn into a checklist, then have it review your own videos against that checklist. You need a ChatGPT or Claude account, the videos or transcripts of creators you respect, and your own videos.
1. Pick a handful of creators whose videos you admire and collect a few of their best videos, as links, transcripts or screen recordings.
1. Give them to ChatGPT or Claude and ask what the videos have in common: how they open, how fast they move, how they are edited and how they close.
1. Ask the assistant to turn those findings into a checklist covering hooks, pacing and style.
1. Add your own video, as a transcript or an upload where the tool accepts video, and ask for a review against the checklist.
1. Ask for the answer as two short lists: "do this" and "stop doing this", each tied to a moment in your video.
1. Apply the changes in your editor, such as CapCut, and run the next video through the same review.
1. Update the checklist as you learn what works for your own audience.
Watch out: the checklist describes what makes other people's videos work, so use it to improve your own style and don't copy their scripts or delivery.

```
You are my video coach. I make short videos about <your topic> for <platform>. I will give you material from creators I admire: <links, transcripts or recordings of their best videos>.
Step 1: Analyse these videos and tell me what they have in common: how they open, how quickly they move, how they are edited and how they end.
Step 2: Turn that into a checklist covering hooks, pacing and style. Keep it to no more than 10 items, each one a clear yes or no question I can check.
Step 3: Review my video, <my transcript or recording>, against the checklist. Return two short lists, "Do this" and "Stop doing this". Tie each point to a specific moment in my video and say what to change.
Keep my own voice and topic. Use the creators for structure and technique only, and do not copy their wording. Write in plain British English with no hype. If you cannot watch video, tell me and ask for transcripts instead.
```
